question:
A Zener diode of Zener voltage $5.6\,\text{V}$ is connected in reverse bias in a regulating circuit.
(a) What voltage will be maintained across the Zener diode when it operates in breakdown region?
(b) Explain why the voltage remains nearly constant even when current changes.

options.A:
(a) In breakdown, the voltage across the Zener diode remains nearly equal to its Zener voltage: $V=V_Z=5.6\,\text{V}$.
(b) In the reverse breakdown region, a large change in current produces only a very small change in voltage. Thus Zener current adjusts with input or load variation while voltage remains nearly constant.
options.B:
(a) The voltage is $0.3\,\text{V}$.
(b) Voltage remains constant because reverse current is always zero.
options.C:
(a) The voltage is $11.2\,\text{V}$.
(b) Voltage doubles whenever Zener current changes.
options.D:
(a) The voltage is zero in the breakdown region.
(b) The Zener diode regulates voltage only in forward bias.
